steps.text: Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Place ribs on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Scatter 4 cloves of sliced garlic over ribs. Cover, and bake for 2 1/2 hours. Cool slightly.
In a small bowl, mix together white sugar, paprika, salt, black pepper, chili powder, and ground cumin. Rub spices over cooled ribs. Cover, and refrigerate overnight.

In a small saucepan, mix together brown sugar, cider vinegar, ketchup, chili sauce, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, onion, dry mustard, and 1 clove garlic. Simmer over medium-low heat, uncovered, for 1 hour. Reserve a small amount for basting; the remainder is a dipping sauce.
Place ribs on grill. Grill, covered, for about 12 minutes, basting with the reserved sauce, until nicely browned and glazed. Serve with remaining sauce for dipping.

raw_recipe.headline: Barbequed Ribs
raw_recipe.description: These pork ribs require a double cooking process and an overnight bath in a marinade. The spicy rub and rich sauce make them worth the wait!

video.description: The secret to great ribs is time—and the wait is totally worth it! Get the ribs ready to soak up flavor by baking them with garlic for a couple of hours. Once cooled, cover them with a spice mixture of sugar, paprika, salt, black pepper, chili powder and cumin. Chill overnight, and just before you’re ready to grill, mix up a basting and dipping sauce of brown sugar, cider vinegar, ketchup, chili sauce, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, onion and dry mustard. Grill up those delicious ribs, baste them well, and serve when brown and glazed. Yum!

review.reviewBody: Believe the hype-- these were fantastic! I don't have a grill so for the grill part, I just put them in the oven at 350 degrees, basting frequently. As recommended, I made double the sauce and didn't leave it over for dipping--- I just slathered the whole amount on there throughout basting! The first time, I didn't listen to others advice and only made the standard amount of sauce. Big mistake! Make double!The sauce was finger-licking good (I mean literally) and I was so pleased that I made my own sauce. No more store-bought-- this one's a keeper! As other people mentioned, I also added a bit of chili pepper flakes for some heat, and it was the perfect balance. Thanks for the recipe for these tender, delicious ribs!

I made this today, followed the instructions to a T except for letting them sit overnight. I cooked them in the oven, let cool for about an hour then rubbed them with the dry rub. (At this point the meat was already falling off the bone) Then straight to the grill basting while grilling them. They were delicious, got compliments from my guests, it's a definable winner that I will make again. I took the advice of previous reviews and doubled the sauce recipe and have a jar in the fridge for the rest of this week.

Absolutely delicious. Baked the ribs in foil packs. Left the sliced garlic on once cooked. Made the rub as is except substituted 1/2 T chipotle chili for regular chili. For the sauce I added a tsp liquid smoke as another reviewer recommended. Good call. Also I accidentally put an entire lemon in so added about 1/8 cup molasses

I’ve made this recipe multiple times and it’s always a hit. There are never any leftovers. I got it from a friend who won a church ribs contest with it! It SOUNDS like a lot of effort, but it’s soooooo worth the 2 day journey, and it’s really not difficult to execute at all- it’s just the overnight marinade post-cooking that makes it seem long. I actually season the raw pork with a homemade adobo the night before baking, so for me it takes 3 days, but the end results are lovely, smokey, delicious ribs with a little kick. The meat just falls off the bone and the sauce melts in your mouth. I actually make double the sauce because my family and friends alway use it for more than just the ribs. They dip veggies in it, mix it in their rice or couscous….. it really is delicious. I’ve even used it on chicken!

Gail must be getting a big head by now but I'll add to it. By leaps and bounds this is the best rib recipe in the world. I know I've not tried them all, but I'd be hard pressed to think there is one better. I have friends who a year or two still beg for them. My change is a make twice the sauce and use it all to slather on there. Makes for wet, dirty get sauce all over your shirt, mouth, and hands ribs but that's a great thing. Cooked mine in the oven. The 2nd day did 240 degrees basting each 10 minutes for 30 - 40 minutes, then 350 uncovered for maybe 15. Last variation is used sweet chili sauce from the asian market. Made it more tangy. Great job Gail!!!

This is a great recipe. I have made this several times now. At first it seemed like a lot of work but I have it down to a science now. First, just slice the garlic in simple slices and put ribs in oven. Second, make the rub. Third, make the sauce and cook it. It will be done before the ribs and stick it in the fridge for the next day. Overnight marinating enhances it. Fourth, when ribs done and cooled add rub and put in fridge for the night. Next day all you have to do is heat sauce, grill ribs, and rake in the yummy compliments.

I used 5lbs of pork country style ribs with the bone in, I sprinkled garlic powder instead of using fresh garlic sparingly over the ribs & cooked them in the oven on 300 for 2.5 hrs. They were a bit greasy, so after they cooled, I wiped them w paper towels & added the rub. I'm not really into really spicy food, so I opted to use 1 tsp of chili powder instead of 2. I tasted a small piece of the rib after I applied the rub... DEEEEEELICIOUS!!!! I

I've made this several times now. The first time, I followed the recipe exactly. My boys loved them and requested often. But it takes planning to make it. I decided to bake, rub then freeze them. When needed all I had to do was to baste and grill. It wasn't as good. 

One day I accidentally I rubbed the ribs first. I then baked and chilled them. The next day I basted and grilled them according to recipe. The ribs tasted so good. Even better then the original. The spices had infused and fused into the meat during baking. 

Since then I've been doing the rub, bake, chill and grill routine. Try it. You'll taste the difference. Don't need to bake with garlic first. Rub with spices and garlic then bake. After baking, don't open the parcel. Leave it to chill till needed the next day. Baste generously and frequently while grilling. Took 10 mins to have a glistening and inviting rack of ribs ready.

Tip: to save electricity, I bake for 1 and 1/2 hours, switche off the oven and leave the ribs to continue cooking (do not open oven door) till oven is cool. Then I just stash ribs in the fridge. The ribs were very tender and only needed 90 mins of baking.

Absolutely great recipe!!!!
The seasonings were perfect!!!
My husband and I had a cook-off to see who could make better ribs, and I won hands down!!
Next time will precook the ribs for 2 hrs @300 instead of 2 1/2 hrs they were already falling off the bone.
I had never made homemade BBQ sauce before until this recipe it turned out great and very easy the only it had to much of an cider vinegar flavor next i will use a 1/2 of a cup. Since the vinegar was so over powering i add more of the other ingredients to calm it down and i also added a dash of liquid smoke it come out perfect!!! I will definitely use this recipe again!!

I use the dry rub, wrap it in plastic wrap and let it sit for the day. Then I grill it on our Primo Grill low and slow for a few hours and baste it at the end with the sauce. Thank you for the wonderful recipie!

Delicious! Took a couple of tips from other reviewers by doubling the amount, adding red pepper flakes, brown sugar, liquid smoke, and mashing the garlic the ribs were baked with before adding the rub. Excellent rib recipe. Thank you!!
Good flavors and easy to do. I may cut back a bit on the cumin next time. The ribs were not quite as tender as some of the other reviewers indicated. Maybe I will bake them a little longer next time.
This was an excellent recipe... tender, flavorful, and smoky. Double the dipping sauce.
Love these ribs. Especially the sauce recipe. Sauce keeps in the fridge for other uses, such as pork slider sandwiches.
These are amazing. I’ve made them 3 times and they are so delicious. The sauce is ridiculously awesome and licked clean each time. I’m critical and me and the family yearn for these. Sweet and tangy.
Huge hit, definitely double the sauce. I wish I made two racks! Quite fantastic, love the recipe.
I’ve tried many rib recipes and this one is the best by far! Remove the tendon on the back of the rib w a sharp knife for even better flavor.
Made these ribs for the fourth!!! Huge hit, especially the kids. Better than Applebees ribs!!! Not sure if that was a compliment or not but I'll take it!! Great recipe!!
Love it.... Thank you for the information. I knew something was missing we I tried to make like my Great-Grand Mother on my Mother side of my family...

Delicious and worth the effort! The meat was very moist and tender and I loved the flavor of the rub. I ran out of time and ended up using bottled bbq sauce, but will definitely try the sauce recipe next time. This recipe is a keeper for sure.
